_README: Regulator enforcement-bulletin feeds — the 4th adverse net (supplementary). Fetched ONCE per run by screen.py (fetch_regulator_bulletins), then every screening subject's significant name tokens are scanned against the item titles/descriptions (screen_regulator_bulletins; >=2 significant tokens required — single-token names stay covered by the fuzzy matcher nets). A regulator naming a subject is a STRONG-tier adverse finding (Enforcement / Legal typology). A feed that fails to fetch is DISCLOSED in the report (section 2 coverage note) and the run log — reduced coverage is never silent and never fatal. This file is OPTIONAL: absent/unreadable means the net is not configured. Feed URLs are best-known-free endpoints; verify on the first live run (the runner egress allowlist in weekly-adverse-media.yml must carry each host). Add feeds via the four-eyes PR procedure; keep entries {name, url, enabled}.

sources.name: US OCC — News Releases (incl. monthly enforcement actions)

_survey_2026_08_05: Worldwide enforcement-feed survey verdicts kept for the record: FinCEN, MAS, FATF (post-2023 site), VARA and OCC's EASearch database publish no RSS/JSON — HTML fingerprinting or curation would be a different net; Eurojust and UNODC advertise RSS but their exact feed URLs were unverifiable from the sandbox — candidates for a follow-up once confirmed from a runner. All five feeds added above are keyless and verify on the first live run (failures are disclosed in §2, never silent).
